briefing: A survey team dug up an I-330 relay. The receiver still works. It caught the last weather report from orbit, including the bit where they promised clear skies.
choice_b: Give the relay to the lab
result_a: Stores took the receiver and its spare casing. They logged {reward}.
result_b: The lab kept the receiver. It recorded {reward} while studying the signal.
offline_a: The survey team found an old I-330 relay. I sent the reusable parts to stores. We gained {reward}.
offline_b: The survey team found an old I-330 relay. I asked the lab to recover its weather recordings. The work yielded {reward}.

briefing: The night crew started setting up stalls outside the freight depot. They did so well on the first night that the day crew came back after their shift. They've offered the colony a share.
choice_a: Take a share of the proceeds
result_a: The night crew transferred {reward} from the stall takings.
result_b: The night crew set aside {reward} for the supply depot.
offline_a: A market opened outside the freight depot while you were gone. I accepted the night crew's offer of a share. They paid us {reward}.
offline_b: A market opened outside the freight depot. I asked the crew to supply the depot. They set aside {reward}.

warning: A crew on {place} cleaned the dust off an antenna this morning. By lunch the coating was back, and their meter was picking up current through it. I asked every grid crew on {place} to check their lines.
briefing: The same dust is bridging power lines across {place}. Crews have traced it into buildings on several separate circuits. If we isolate those lines now, the affected sites will lose part of their power output for two months. If we hold the grid open, crews will have to abandon any buildings they can no longer reach safely.
result_a: Crews isolated the affected lines. Energy output on {place} will be 25% lower for two months while the dust settles.
mitigation_tip: Protect the buildings by shutting off the affected lines.
followup_text_a: The crews on {place} kept the insulation we removed during the storm. They've finally reproduced the dust shorts in the lab and filed a report worth {reward}.
followup_text_b: The next dust front passed well clear of {place}. When the warning came through, crews went back over the buildings we left on the live lines last time. They know which doors they can reach from the ground now.
followup_text_emergency: The emergency crews on {place} kept the readings from the storm. The lab used them to map how the dust travelled between live lines. Their report yielded {reward}.

warning: The harbour crew in {place} found their low-tide markers underwater this week. The survey team rechecked the levels. There's a surge coming, and our lowest streets are in its path.
briefing: Water is already coming up through the drains in {place}. The crews can build a temporary barrier if we hand over supplies now. Otherwise they'll clear the waterfront and leave the buildings inside the flood line to take the surge.
result_a: The crews used our supplies to close the breach before the surge reached the buildings in {place}.
followup_text_a: The breakwater crew reused the foundation we laid in {place} during the flood. That saved them a shipment of material. They returned {reward} from the project budget.
followup_text_b: The survey team finished the new flood map for {place}. It includes the streets we had to clear during the surge. The old high-water marks are still there on the stairs.
followup_text_emergency: The pumps we used in {place} are back from the waterfront. The harbour crew sold the salvaged fittings and transferred {reward} to the treasury.
